concrete_examples.description: In NetHack, players can learn spells through spellbooks and cast them by consuming magic points (mana) from their resource pool. The game requires players to manage their spellcasting by balancing the use of spells with the limited availability of mana and the need to conserve it for critical moments.

In broguece, players can learn spells by finding spellbooks, each spell consuming a certain amount of mana when cast. The game incorporates a resource management system, where players must balance their mana usage with the need to explore and survive in the roguelike environment.

In 'Crawl', the magic and spellcasting system allows players to learn spells from books and cast them using a resource called 'mana'. Players must manage their mana effectively, as casting spells depletes this resource, requiring strategic decisions about which spells to use in combat and exploration.

In cataclysm-bn, the magic and spellcasting system allows players to learn various spells that consume resources like mana. Players must strategically manage their mana pool to decide when to cast powerful spells during combat or exploration, creating a dynamic resource management challenge.

definition: A game mechanic where players can learn and cast spells that consume resources (mana, spell slots, hunger, etc.). Magic provides powerful tactical options but creates resource management decisions about when and what to cast.
exclusion_criteria: Innate abilities that don't consume resources
Consumable-only items without a spell system
Magic that is purely cosmetic without gameplay impact
inclusion_criteria: Player can learn or acquire spells
Casting spells consumes a resource (mana, spell slots, hunger, etc.)
Spells provide tactical options not available through melee/ranged combat
Spell selection creates strategic loadout decisions
title: Magic and Spellcasting System
